claims.explanation: NSC-663284 is a quinone-based Cdc25 inhibitor that also redox cycles to generate reactive oxygen species, and its selectivity likely reflects dependence on Cdc25/cyclin-dependent kinase activity plus sensitivity to oxidative stress. Lines with intact oxidative-stress response pathways (e.g., KEAP1/NRF2/NFE2L2 mutations) may survive better, while those with high Cdc25A/B/C expression or loss of cell-cycle checkpoints (e.g., TP53 mutation) are more sensitive. The observed enrichment of BRAF-mutant melanoma and RAS-pathway-mutant lines among sensitive lines suggests that MAPK-driven proliferation increases dependence on Cdc25 and/or ROS-mediated inhibition of phosphatases.

features.basis: NSC-663284 directly inhibits Cdc25A (Ki 29 nM); high expression increases dependence
NSC-663284 is most selective for Cdc25B (Ki 95 nM); high expression increases dependence
NSC-663284 inhibits Cdc25C (Ki 89 nM); high expression increases dependence
Loss of KEAP1 activates NRF2 and antioxidant response, countering ROS-mediated killing; KEAP1-mutant lines are among least affected
Activating NFE2L2 mutations increase antioxidant capacity, reducing ROS-mediated toxicity; NFE2L2-mutant lines are less sensitive
TP53 loss impairs DNA damage/oxidative stress checkpoints, enhancing sensitivity; most sensitive lines carry TP53 mutations
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines are enriched among sensitive lines, possibly via MAPK-driven proliferation and Cdc25 dependence
NRAS-mutant lines (NCIH1299, SW1088, KU1919) are among sensitive lines, suggesting RAS/MAPK pathway activation increases sensitivity
KRAS-mutant lines are present among sensitive lines, though also among resistant, so weaker evidence
SMARCA4-mutant lines (COV434, KYSE270) are sensitive, but also seen in resistant lines, so weak
ARID1A mutations appear in both sensitive and resistant lines, but several resistant lines carry ARID1A mutations, suggesting possible protection
SF3B1 mutations are enriched in resistant lines (LS1034, CAL12T, HCC95, TE4, SNUC5), suggesting spliceosome mutations may reduce sensitivity
